question: What test is used where the elements present in the compound are converted from covalent form into the ionic form by fusing the compound with sodium metal?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Lassaigne's test.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lassaigne's test** is a general test for the detection of halogens, nitrogen, and sulfur in an organic compound.
 
• These elements are covalently bonded to the organic compounds. 
 
• In order to detect them, these have to be converted into their ionic forms.
 
• This is done by fusing the organic compound with sodium metal. This is done by fusing the organic compound with sodium metal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A flame test is an analytical procedure used in chemistry to detect the presence of certain elements, primarily metal ions, based on each element's characteristic emission spectrum. 
 
• A D-dimer test looks for D-dimer in blood. D-dimer is a protein fragment (small piece) that's made when a blood clot dissolves in your body.
